title: compute/v1 sandbox join file
description: /etc/agentcompute/network.json in a sandbox this layer created: everything the client (AgentDevice `agentdevice sandbox`) needs to join the owner's NetBird network and serve SSH without a person, no login and no enrolment call. Written once per sandbox by this layer, mode 0600, owned by `user`. It holds secrets (the one-use setup key, the SSH host key): never logged, never on a command line (R21). README.md §7.1.

version.description: This file's version; absent in the first files (managementUrl, deviceName, setupKey only).

computer.description: The sandbox's computer id: SSH tokens must cover computer:<this>:ssh.

own.description: The owner: SSH tokens must carry this `own`.

ten.description: The tenant: SSH tokens must carry this `ten`.

issuer.description: identity/v1 issuer (`iss`); its key set is <issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json.

deviceName.description: The NetBird peer name: the computer id.

setupKey.description: One-use NetBird setup key of the owner's account (expires in 24 h). Spent at the first join; later starts reuse the peer key the client saved.

hostKey.description: The SSH host key the client serves with (Ed25519, PKCS#8 or OpenSSH PEM). This layer generates it, so its public half is the computer's `hostKey` in the access answer from the start.

user.description: The account the client runs as and every SSH session runs as (the access answer's `user`).

tokenMaxAgeSeconds.description: How old (now - iat) an SSH token may be; default 600.

proxy.description: The sandbox's only egress is an HTTP CONNECT proxy (a Daytona node's). NetBird's relay dialer does not use proxies, so: this layer maps each of `hosts` to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts and lets unprivileged users bind port 443; the client listens on `listen` and relays each TLS connection whose SNI is one of `hosts` through the proxy (CONNECT <sni>:443); its own HTTPS calls use the proxy directly.

hosts.description: NetBird's management, signal and relay host names (port 443).
